observation.visible_scene: A yellow steel truss bridge (the Victoria Falls Bridge) crosses the frame horizontally, with a grey lower deck structure beneath it. A white tour van lettered 'Bumpy Travels' sits on the bridge deck, with several passengers leaning out of its open rear/side windows, legs dangling. Small pedestrians are on the footway beside the railing. Behind the bridge is a forested cliff/hill topped by a single broad tree, and pale mist from waterfalls hangs in the sky and along the left side.
visible_changes: The framing shifts over the clip: the forested hill and the lone tree move toward the right edge and partly out of view, while a covered viewing platform with people on it enters from the left edge, indicating camera movement across the scene.

Pedestrians change position relative to the van and to the bridge structure; two pedestrians initially to the right of the van progress rightward and leave the frame, while other pedestrians (including one in a white shirt) appear from the left and move along the footway.
The white van's position relative to the bridge truss changes only modestly, drifting slowly along the deck; the passengers leaning from its windows keep roughly the same pose throughout.
The mist/waterfall spray on the left side drifts and changes shape, becoming denser in places.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the van is driving, idling, or stopped, and the direction/origin of its travel along the bridge.
Whether the pedestrians are entering or leaving the bridge, and their destinations.
The full extent of the viewing platform and what happens on it.
The cause of the mist and the overall waterfall layout beyond the left edge.
uncertain_details: The exact split between camera motion and object motion: the bridge columns and the background hill appear to shift in opposite directions across the clip, so the camera may be panning/trucking with parallax, and the van's true motion relative to the bridge cannot be confirmed from these frames alone.
Whether the van is moving or stationary relative to the deck is not decisively supported.
